20 Library: jsx-graph🔗

 (include-lib jsx-graph)

 Compile option:  --ffi jsxgraph

The jsx-graph library provides a small Rackety wrapper around JSXGraph board and element construction. JSXGraph is an interactive geometry system for drawing points, lines, circles, surfaces, and other constructions on a browser board.

Use jsx-graph when you want to:

  • create a JXG.JSXGraph board in the current page

  • create arbitrary JSXGraph elements with jsx-create or the specialized constructors

  • create 3D scenes with jsx-create-view3d and the 3D helpers for points, lines, circles, planes, axes, function graphs, spheres, surfaces, curves, polyhedra, text, ticks, transformations, and vector fields

  • build geometry objects such as JXG.Point, JXG.Line, JXG.Arc, JXG.Angle, JXG.Sector, JXG.Circle, JXG.Conic, JXG.Ellipse, JXG.Functiongraph, JXG.Riemannsum, JXG.Slopefield, JXG.Vectorfield, JXG.ImplicitCurve, JXG.Spline, JXG.Cardinalspline, JXG.Comb, JXG.Metapostspline, JXG.PolygonalChain, JXG.RegularPolygon, JXG.Hyperbola, JXG.Parabola, JXG.Stepfunction, JXG.Inequality, JXG.Turtle, JXG.Polygon, JXG.Text, JXG.ForeignObject, JXG.Tapemeasure, JXG.Hatch, JXG.Measurement, JXG.Circumcenter, JXG.Incenter, JXG.MinorArc, JXG.MinorSector, JXG.NonReflexAngle, JXG.Slopetriangle, and JXG.MirrorElement

  • create chart objects with JXG.Chart

  • create legends and smart labels

  • create widget-like elements such as buttons, checkboxes, sliders, and inputs

  • inspect or adjust point properties from Racket code

  • attach browser event handlers to JSXGraph elements

The library keeps the browser FFI bindings behind checked helper functions. For the underlying js-jsx-* bindings, see ffi/jsxgraph.ffi and the corresponding browser API reference page.

The main constructors return checked wrapper structs: jsx-board for JSXGraph boards, jsx-point for point values, and jsx-element for other geometry objects.

Type notes for the wrapped API:

  • Board and element arguments use the checked wrappers in the public API.

  • Constructor parents are usually packed with jsx-parents and therefore arrive as vectors.

  • Special constructors that accept callable parents are documented explicitly below.

  • Constructor attributes are JSXGraph option objects, usually built with jsx-attributes.

  • A few low-level geometry hooks intentionally stay broad because JSXGraph forwards browser values through them.

  • jsx-parents is the intended variadic packing boundary, so it accepts mixed raw values and checked wrappers.

  • jsx-point? is a predicate over any value, so its argument stays broad by design.

20.1 Quick Start🔗

Start by including the library, making a board, and adding a pair of points and a line between them.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(define p (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents -1 0)))
(define q (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents 1 0)))
(define l (jsx-create-line board (jsx-parents p q)))
 
(void board p q l)

The quick start uses jsx-parents to pack the parent values into the vector shape JSXGraph expects, and jsx-attributes to build option objects when you need them.

Use jsx-parents for constructor inputs that describe geometry relationships, such as points, parent elements, or callable parents. Use jsx-attributes for option objects that control appearance or behavior, such as names, colors, sizes, grids, and board settings.

A board with explicit options looks like this:

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board
  (jsx-create-board "box"
                    (jsx-attributes
                      [boundingbox #[-5 5 5 -5]]
                      [axis #t]
                      [grid #t]
                      [keepaspectratio #t])))

20.2 Common Patterns🔗

The most common JSXGraph tasks in this library fall into a few simple patterns.

20.2.1 Board, Points, And Line🔗

Create a board, place two points, and connect them with a line.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(define p (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents -1 0)))
(define q (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents 1 0)))
(define l (jsx-create-line board (jsx-parents p q)))
 
(void board p q l)

20.2.2 Board Options🔗

Use jsx-attributes for board options such as the bounding box, axes, and grid.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board
  (jsx-create-board "box"
                    (jsx-attributes
                      [boundingbox #[-5 5 5 -5]]
                      [axis #t]
                      [grid #t]
                      [keepaspectratio #t])))

20.2.3 3D View🔗

Create a 3D scene inside a normal board, then add a 3D point.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box3d"))
(define view
  (jsx-create-view3d board
                     (jsx-parents (vector -4 -3)
                                  (vector 8 8)
                                  (vector (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)))
                     (jsx-attributes [projection "parallel"])))
(define p
  (jsx-view3d-create-point3d view (vector 1 2 2)
                             (jsx-attributes [name "A"])))
(void board view p)

procedure

(jsx-create-view3d board parents [attributes]) → jsx-element?

  board : jsx-board?
  parents : any/c
  attributes : (or/c #f external/raw) = #f

 JSXGraph  View3D

Creates a 3D scene inside a board.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box3d"))
(define view
  (jsx-create-view3d board
                     (jsx-parents (vector -4 -3)
                                  (vector 8 8)
                                  (vector (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)))
                     (jsx-attributes [projection "parallel"])))

20.2.4 Event Handler🔗

Attach a browser event handler to a board or geometry element.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(jsx-board-add-event!
 board
 "mousedown"
 (lambda args
   (console-log "board clicked")))

20.3 Parent Shapes🔗

Use jsx-parents when a constructor needs geometry parents.

  • For points, pass a coordinate pair such as (jsx-parents -1 0).

  • For lines and polygons, pass parent points or a vector/list of points.

  • For Curve and Functiongraph, a callable parent is also allowed.

20.4 Option Objects🔗

Use jsx-attributes for JSXGraph option objects.

  • Board: boundingbox, axis, grid, keepaspectratio.

  • Point and line: name, size, face, strokeColor, dash, straightFirst, straightLast.

  • 3D view: projection, trackball, and the plane visibility flags used by JSXGraph’s 3D view options.

syntax

(jsx-attributes [key value] ...)

Build a JSXGraph option object from option-style pairs.

Each key should be an option name. In practice that is usually written as an identifier, but strings and symbols also work. Each value may be any expression, including nested jsx-attributes forms.

Kebab-style option names such as straight-first and stroke-color are rewritten to the camelCase spellings that JSXGraph expects. Plain all-lowercase names such as boundingbox stay unchanged.

Common board options include:

  • boundingbox for the visible board rectangle

  • axis to show or hide the coordinate axes

  • grid to show or hide the board grid

  • keepaspectratio to lock the board aspect ratio

The same form also works for element option objects, for example:
(jsx-attributes
  [name "A"]
  [size 4]
  [visible #t]
  [stroke-color "crimson"])

For a point, the same style can be used with the point constructor:

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(define p
  (jsx-create-point board
                    (jsx-parents -1 0)
                    (jsx-attributes
                      [name "A"]
                      [size 4]
                      [face "o"]
                      [stroke-color "crimson"])))

For a line, the same pattern gives you a styled segment or infinite line depending on the line options:

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(define p (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents -1 0)))
(define q (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents 1 0)))
(define l
  (jsx-create-line board
                   (jsx-parents p q)
                   (jsx-attributes
                     [straight-first #t]
                     [straight-last #t]
                     [stroke-color "crimson"]
[dash 2])))
]

20.5 Gallery Map🔗

The gallery in lib/web-easy/examples/jsx-graph-gallery/jsx-graph-gallery.rkt shows the same ideas in separate boards. Use it as a visual index when you want to see a constructor family in action before reading the full reference entry.

  • Geometry basics: the geometry, point, line, arc, angle, sector, circle, and glider boards show the core 2D constructors.

  • Construction helpers: midpoint, parallel, perpendicular, reflection, bisector, incircle, incenter, minor arc, minor sector, non-reflex angle, hatch, measurement, circumcenter, and related helper boards show the derived constructions.

  • Widgets and text: the widgets, annotation, button, checkbox, input, slider, smartlabel, foreign object, image, tape measure, and text boards show the UI-style elements.

  • Analysis and curves: the functiongraph, curve, derivative, integral, riemannsum, slopefield, vectorfield, implicitcurve, spline, cardinalspline, comb, metapostspline, and polygonal chain boards show sampled and analytic curves.

  • 3D: the view3d, point3d, line3d, circle3d, plane3d, axes3d, axis3d, functiongraph3d, curve3d, surface3d, parametricsurface3d, polyhedron3d, face3d, ticks3d, transformation3d, and vectorfield3d boards show the 3D view and its scene elements.

  • Use jsx-attributes for styling and behavior options, not for geometry parents.

  • Use jsx-parents for geometry relationships, not for appearance options.

  • Put 3D view options on jsx-create-view3d, not on the outer board.

20.8 3D Geometry🔗

The 3D helpers build on top of a normal JSXGraph board and a 3D view inside that board. The outer board provides the browser container, and the 3D view supplies the actual 3D scene. A compact example is:

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box3d"))
(define view
  (jsx-create-view3d board
                     (jsx-parents (vector -4 -3)
                                  (vector 8 8)
                                  (vector (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)))
                     (jsx-attributes [projection "parallel"])))
(define p
  (jsx-view3d-create-point3d view (vector 1 2 2)
                             (jsx-attributes [name "A"])))
(void board view p)

The dedicated gallery section uses the 3D helpers to show views, primitives, intersections, curves, surfaces, solids, and other 3D element types in separate example boards.

When you configure a 3D view, use jsx-attributes for the options object on the view itself. The surrounding board still uses the usual board options if you want to change its 2D container behavior.

In practice that means:

  • jsx-create-board takes the outer container options such as boundingbox, axis, and grid.

  • jsx-create-view3d takes the inner scene options such as projection, trackball, and the 3D plane visibility flags.

Common 3D view options include projection for the projection mode, trackball for interactive rotation, and the rear-plane visibility options that control how much of the 2D backdrop you see. For example:

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box3d"))
(jsx-create-view3d board
                   (jsx-parents (vector -4 -3)
                                (vector 8 8)
                                (vector (vector -5 5)
                                        (vector -5 5)
                                        (vector -5 5)))
                   (jsx-attributes
                     [projection "central"]
                     [trackball (jsx-attributes [enabled #t])]))

Common 3D view attributes are:

Attribute

Meaning

projection

Chooses the projection mode, such as parallel or central.

trackball

Controls interactive 3D rotation and related interaction settings.

axes-position

Chooses where the 3D axes appear.

x-plane-rear

Configures the rear x-plane backdrop.

y-plane-rear

Configures the rear y-plane backdrop.

z-plane-rear

Configures the rear z-plane backdrop.

20.8.1 3D Helper Constructors🔗

These constructors cover the 3D helpers that are most naturally used as scene-local elements inside a 3D view.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box3d"))
(define view
  (jsx-create-view3d board
                     (jsx-parents (vector -4 -3)
                                  (vector 8 8)
                                  (vector (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)))))
(jsx-view3d-create-point3d view (vector 1 2 2))
20.8.1.1 3D Primitives🔗

  • jsx-view3d-create-point3d creates a 3D point. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-point3d view (vector 1 2 2)).

  • jsx-view3d-create-line3d creates a 3D line. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-line3d view (jsx-parents a b)).

  • jsx-view3d-create-circle3d creates a 3D circle. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-circle3d view (jsx-parents a (vector 0 0 0 1) 2)).

  • jsx-view3d-create-plane3d creates a 3D plane. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-plane3d view (jsx-parents a b c)).

  • jsx-view3d-create-axes3d creates a 3D axes frame. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-axes3d view (jsx-parents)).

  • jsx-view3d-create-axis3d creates a single 3D axis. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-axis3d view (jsx-parents (vector -2 -2 -2) (vector 3 3 3))).

  • jsx-view3d-create-functiongraph3d creates a 3D function graph. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-functiongraph3d view (jsx-parents (lambda (x y) (sin (/ (* x y) 4))) (vector -5 5) (vector -5 5))).

  • jsx-view3d-create-sphere3d creates a 3D sphere. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-sphere3d view (jsx-parents a b)).

  • jsx-view3d-create-curve3d creates a 3D curve. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-curve3d view (jsx-parents (lambda (t) (cos t)) (lambda (t) (sin t)) (lambda (t) (/ t 4)) (vector 0 (* 2 pi)))).

  • jsx-view3d-create-text3d creates 3D text. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-text3d view (vector 0 0 0 "3D text")).

  • jsx-view3d-create-ticks3d creates 3D tick marks. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-ticks3d view (jsx-parents (vector -4 0 0) (vector 1 0 0) 6 (vector 0 0 1))).

  • jsx-view3d-create-vectorfield3d creates a 3D vector field. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-vectorfield3d view (jsx-parents (vector (lambda (x y z) (cos y)) (lambda (x y z) (sin x)) (lambda (x y z) z)) (vector -2 5 2) (vector -2 5 2) (vector -2 5 2))).

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box3d"))
(define view
  (jsx-create-view3d board
                     (jsx-parents (vector -4 -3)
                                  (vector 8 8)
                                  (vector (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)))))
(define a (jsx-view3d-create-point3d view (vector 1 2 2)))
(define b (jsx-view3d-create-point3d view (vector -2 -1 -1)))
(define c (jsx-view3d-create-point3d view (vector 0 3 0)))
 
 
(jsx-view3d-create-point3d view (vector 1 2 2))
 
 
(jsx-view3d-create-line3d view (jsx-parents a b))

(jsx-view3d-create-plane3d view (jsx-parents a b c))

                                            (vector 3 3 3)))

 view
 (jsx-parents (lambda (x y) (sin (/ (* x y) 4)))
              (vector -5 5)
              (vector -5 5)))

20.8.1.2 3D Surfaces And Solids🔗

  • jsx-view3d-create-face3d creates a polyhedron face. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-face3d view (jsx-parents polyhedron-def 0)).

  • jsx-view3d-create-surface3d creates a 3D parametric surface. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-surface3d view (jsx-parents (lambda (u v) (* 2 (cos u) (cos v))) (lambda (u v) (* 1.5 (sin u) (cos v))) (lambda (u v) (* 0.75 (sin v))) (vector 0 (* 2 pi)) (vector -1.5 1.5))).

  • jsx-view3d-create-parametricsurface3d creates a 3D parametric surface. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-parametricsurface3d view (jsx-parents (lambda (u v) (* 2 (sin u) (cos v))) (lambda (u v) (* 2 (sin u) (sin v))) (lambda (u v) (* 2 (cos u))) (vector 0 (* 2 pi)) (vector 0 pi))).

  • jsx-view3d-create-polyhedron3d creates a 3D polyhedron. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-polyhedron3d view (jsx-parents (vector (vector -3 -3 -3) (vector 3 -3 -3) (vector 3 3 -3) (vector -3 3 -3) (vector -3 -3 3) (vector 3 -3 3) (vector 3 3 3) (vector -3 3 3)) (vector (vector 0 1 2 3) (vector 4 5 6 7) (vector 0 1 5 4) (vector 1 2 6 5) (vector 2 3 7 6) (vector 3 0 4 7)))).

  • jsx-view3d-create-transformation3d creates a 3D transformation helper. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-transformation3d view (vector 1.5 0.75 0.5) (jsx-attributes [type "translate"])).

                        (vector -3 -3 3)
                        (vector 3 -3 3)
                        (vector 3 3 3)
                        (vector -3 3 3))
                (vector (vector 0 1 2 3)
                        (vector 4 5 6 7)
                        (vector 0 1 5 4)
                        (vector 1 2 6 5)
                        (vector 2 3 7 6)
                        (vector 3 0 4 7)))))
(define polyhedron-def (js-ref (jsx-element-raw polyhedron) "def"))
 
 
(jsx-view3d-create-face3d view (jsx-parents polyhedron-def 0))
 
 
(jsx-view3d-create-surface3d
 view
 (jsx-parents (lambda (u v) (* 2 (cos u) (cos v)))
              (lambda (u v) (* 1.5 (sin u) (cos v)))
              (lambda (u v) (* 0.75 (sin v)))
              (vector 0 (* 2 pi))
              (vector -1.5 1.5)))
 
 
(jsx-view3d-create-parametricsurface3d
 view
 (jsx-parents (lambda (u v) (* 2 (sin u) (cos v)))
              (lambda (u v) (* 2 (sin u) (sin v)))
              (lambda (u v) (* 2 (cos u)))
              (vector 0 (* 2 pi))
              (vector 0 pi)))
 
 
(jsx-view3d-create-polyhedron3d
 view
 (jsx-parents (vector (vector -3 -3 -3)
                      (vector 3 -3 -3)
                      (vector 3 3 -3)
                      (vector -3 3 -3)
                      (vector -3 -3 3)
                      (vector 3 -3 3)
                      (vector 3 3 3)
                      (vector -3 3 3))
              (vector (vector 0 1 2 3)
                      (vector 4 5 6 7)
                      (vector 0 1 5 4)
                      (vector 1 2 6 5)
                      (vector 2 3 7 6)
                      (vector 3 0 4 7))))
 
 
(define transform (jsx-view3d-create-transformation3d
                    view
                    (vector 1.5 0.75 0.5)
                    (jsx-attributes [type "translate"])))
(jsx-view3d-create-point3d view
                           (jsx-parents sphere-a transform))
20.8.1.3 3D Intersections🔗

  • jsx-view3d-create-intersectioncircle3d creates the circle intersection of two 3D solids. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-intersectioncircle3d view (jsx-parents sphere-1 sphere-2)).

  • jsx-view3d-create-intersectionline3d creates the line intersection of two 3D planes. Minimal example: (jsx-view3d-create-intersectionline3d view (jsx-parents plane-1 plane-2)).

procedure

(jsx-view3d-create-intersectioncircle3d view 
  parents 
  [attributes]) 
 → jsx-element?
  view : jsx-element?
  parents : any/c
  attributes : (or/c #f external/raw) = #f

 JSXGraph  intersectioncircle3d

Creates the circle intersection of two 3D solids inside a 3D view.

procedure

(jsx-view3d-create-intersectionline3d view 
  parents 
  [attributes]) 
 → jsx-element?
  view : jsx-element?
  parents : any/c
  attributes : (or/c #f external/raw) = #f

 JSXGraph  intersectionline3d

Creates the line intersection of two 3D planes inside a 3D view.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box3d"))
(define view
  (jsx-create-view3d board
                     (jsx-parents (vector -4 -3)
                                  (vector 8 8)
                                  (vector (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)
                                          (vector -5 5)))))
(define sphere-1 (jsx-view3d-create-sphere3d view (jsx-parents (vector -1 0 0) 2)))
(define sphere-2 (jsx-view3d-create-sphere3d view (jsx-parents (vector 1 0 0) 2)))
(define plane-1 (jsx-view3d-create-plane3d view (jsx-parents (vector 2 2 0)
                                                              (vector 1 0 0)
                                                              (vector 0 1 0))))
(define plane-2 (jsx-view3d-create-plane3d view (jsx-parents (vector 2 2 0)
                                                              (vector -2 1 1)
                                                              (vector 1 -2 1))))
 
 
(jsx-view3d-create-intersectioncircle3d view
                                        (jsx-parents sphere-1 sphere-2))
 
 
(jsx-view3d-create-intersectionline3d view
                                      (jsx-parents plane-1 plane-2))

20.9 2D Geometry🔗

This section groups the core 2D constructors by family, from the smallest geometric objects up through curves, graphs, polygons, and special relation objects.

20.9.1 Boards, Points, And Lines🔗

This family covers the board container and the basic point and line constructors.

struct

(struct jsx-board (raw)
    #:extra-constructor-name make-jsx-board)
  raw : external/raw
Wraps a JSXGraph board object.

struct

(struct jsx-element (raw)
    #:extra-constructor-name make-jsx-element)
  raw : external/raw
Wraps a generic JSXGraph geometry object.

struct

(struct jsx-point (raw)
    #:extra-constructor-name make-jsx-point)
  raw : external/raw
Wraps a JSXGraph point object.

procedure

(jsx-create-board container-id    
  [maybe-attributes]) → jsx-board?
  container-id : string?
  maybe-attributes : (or/c #f external/raw) = #f

 JSXGraph  JXG.JSXGraph

Creates a JSXGraph board for the container with the given id. Pass #f for the default board options or a raw JSXGraph option object, usually built with jsx-attributes.

Board options commonly include:

  • boundingbox for the visible board rectangle

  • axis to show or hide the coordinate axes

  • grid to show or hide the board grid

  • keepaspectratio to lock the board aspect ratio

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))

procedure

(jsx-create board    
  element-type    
  parents    
  [attributes]) → jsx-element?
  board : jsx-board?
  element-type : (or/c string? symbol?)
  parents : vector?
  attributes : (or/c #f external/raw) = #f

 JSXGraph  JXG.Board

Creates a JSXGraph element of the requested type on board. Pass jsx-attributes output for attributes when you want to set names, colors, sizes, or other element options.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(define p (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents 0 0)))
(define q (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents 1 0)))
(define l (jsx-create board 'line (jsx-parents p q)))

procedure

(jsx-create-point board parents [attributes]) → jsx-point?

  board : jsx-board?
  parents : vector?
  attributes : (or/c #f external/raw) = #f

 JSXGraph  Point

Creates a point, either free or constrained by parents. Use jsx-attributes for the optional point attributes.

Point attributes commonly include:

  • name for the displayed label

  • size for the marker size

  • face for the marker shape

  • fill-color for the marker fill color

  • stroke-color for the marker outline color

  • visible to show or hide the point

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(define p (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents 0 0)))

procedure

(jsx-create-line board parents [attributes]) → jsx-element?

  board : jsx-board?
  parents : vector?
  attributes : (or/c #f external/raw) = #f

 JSXGraph  Line

Creates a line from parent points or a callable parent. Use jsx-attributes for the optional line attributes.

Line attributes commonly include:

  • straight-first to extend the line beyond the first parent point

  • straight-last to extend the line beyond the second parent point

  • stroke-color for the line color

  • dash for the dash style

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(define p (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents -1 0)))
(define q (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents 1 0)))
(define l (jsx-create-line board (jsx-parents p q)))

20.9.2 Curves, Circles, And Graphs🔗

This family covers the common continuous geometry constructors such as segments, arcs, circles, curves, and function graphs.

These constructors are the ones you reach for when the object is a single geometric shape or a graph-like curve rather than a helper construction.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(define p (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents -1 0)))
(define q (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents 1 0)))
(define line (jsx-create-line board (jsx-parents p q)))
20.9.2.1 Segments, Arcs, Angles, And Gliders🔗

20.10.6 Chart Helpers🔗

The jsx-chart wrappers expose the documented JXG.Chart draw and update methods. These methods mirror the JSXGraph API closely and return the raw browser result.

(include-lib jsx-graph)

20.10.7 ForeignObject Helpers🔗

The jsx-foreignobject wrappers expose the documented JXG.ForeignObject methods that are specific to embedded HTML content inside a JSXGraph board.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(define fo
  (jsx-create-foreignobject
   board
   (jsx-parents "<div>ForeignObject</div>"
                (jsx-parents -3 1)
                (jsx-parents 220 80))))

20.10.8 Text Helpers🔗

The jsx-text wrappers expose the documented JXG.Text methods that are specific to text elements. Inherited geometry and coordinate helpers are provided through the generic jsx-element wrappers.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(define p (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents 0 0)))
(define txt (jsx-create-text board (jsx-parents p 1 1 "Hello")))
(jsx-text-set-text! txt "World")

20.12 Board and Element Methods🔗

This section collects the wrappers that operate on boards, geometry elements, and the shared geometry-element API.

The jsx-element wrapper covers JSXGraph geometry elements and compositions. The methods below mirror the documented JXG.GeometryElement API where it is useful from Racket. Some low-level hooks are intentionally left broad because JSXGraph itself forwards raw browser values through them.

20.13 Low-Level Notes🔗

These forms are the lowest-level wrappers in the library and are kept intentionally broad when JSXGraph itself accepts a wide range of values.

The forms below are the intentionally broad boundary helpers. They accept raw browser values or pass them through to JSXGraph with only light wrapping.

(include-lib jsx-graph)
 
(define board (jsx-create-board "box"))
(define p (jsx-create-point board (jsx-parents 0 0)))
(jsx-parents p (vector 1 1))
(jsx-coordinates p)

procedure

(jsx-parents v ...) → vector?

  v : any/c
Packs parent values into a vector for JSXGraph.

This is the intended variadic packing boundary, so it accepts checked wrappers, raw browser values, vectors, lists, and callable parent forms.
